openings.claim: Two removable bolted strip saddles could carry retention formerly supplied by straps, while their visible jaw gaps turn the adverse card into a closure-control signal.
openings.delta: Pair the four strips into two padded edge clamps; drill only strips, place bolts outside hatch/rim edges, and tether removable parts with cord. New carrier: strip-and-bolt interfaces transmit separation resistance into the rim. Card at right contact → increased right jaw gap → marked gap mismatch → technician loosens the left clamp and recenters before retightening. This changes the independent-tightening action; it does not assume the card can be mechanically accommodated.
openings.prediction: Nearest rival: ordinary independent clamping merely holds the hatch harder and reproduces opposite-corner lift. The proposed response predicts lower opposite-corner lift after gap-triggered adjustment while retaining position and pull resistance. Equal improvement without gap information favors the rival explanation of simple preload reduction. A sham gap signal causing unnecessary adjustment defeats signal specificity.
openings.probe: First verify accessible opposing rim surfaces, bolt reach, recoverable attachment and seal-safe pad locations; absence stops fabrication. Within ninety minutes build one configuration. Use up to twelve closure/pull trials: ten opening cycles, including a sham external gap indication followed by its removal, and a final actual right-card closure; reserve two trials for adjustment comparisons before that final closure. Record position, corner lift, 20 N displacement, reopening time and tears. Test signal cancellation by removing the sham. Reject on binding, false signals, unavailable geometry, any constraint breach or failed final outcomes; stopping alone establishes no feasibility.
assumptions: Rim underside access, edge overlap and supplied bolt lengths are unknown and indispensable.
Gap indication must distinguish card-induced lift from clamp flex or pad compression; this is unproven.

Maintenance costs include checking bolts, pads, marks and tethers each cycle. The technician retains fabrication, interpretation, preload adjustment, recentering, component recovery and seal inspection responsibility.
The seal may not accommodate the card without violating the outcome; no performance is established.

assessment: One exploratory opening, not deployment. Both relocation and disturbance conversion depend on unverified geometry and informative gap sensing; preserve every hard constraint.
